solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Finally abridged book of maps

indicators.note: abridged means cut short, so the final letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: finally means at last, run together as one string of letters

explanation.surface: A cartographic volume has at last been cut down to size.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Finally' looks like an instruction to take a last letter, but it is the phrase AT LAST, which 'abridged' trims of its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A bound collection of maps is the standard meaning of the word.

clue.text: Pain in course of stomach exercises

indicators.note: the letters run in the course of the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: Sit-ups and crunches leave the abdomen sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in course of' signals letters hidden across 'stomach exercises', spanning the end of one word and the start of the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A dull continuous hurt is a synonym of pain.

clue.text: Many which will appear in auctions

definitions.meaning: a large number, as in plenty of something
the numbered items put up for sale one at a time at an auction

explanation.surface: Plenty of items come up for sale at auction houses.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a great deal informally, and also the individual items offered for bidding.

clue.text: Football fan has to drink dark ale

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in small mouthfuls
porter is a dark brown beer brewed from charred malt

explanation.surface: A football follower is obliged to down a stout before the match.
explanation.walkthrough: PORTER is a dark beer historically popular with London porters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who follows and backs a team is its fan, a common sports usage.

clue.text: Threatened fix involves good service

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the repair word wraps around the tennis term

parts.note: to fix something is to mend it
in tennis an ace is a serve the opponent cannot touch

explanation.surface: A repair job involves decent customer service, apparently under threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good service' is tennis, not shop counters: a serve the opponent cannot return.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimidated or put at risk are the past-tense senses shared by both words.

clue.text: Dark red jumper chap's carrying

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the chap wraps around the jumper

parts.note: a chap is a man; the 's stands for has, linking to carrying
a jumper is a kangaroo, shortened to roo

explanation.surface: A man is wearing a crimson sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater, but here it is the Australian hopping animal; 'carrying' signals the enclosure.
explanation.definitionFit: A brownish-crimson colour goes by this name, the same sense as the noun.

clue.text: Part of pen made from scrap that's turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to scrap something is to bin it, throw it away

explanation.surface: A pen component has been fashioned from a recycled oddment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses BIN, since in a down clue up means backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The metal writing point of a fountain pen is one of its parts.

clue.text: Tea taken with rather uninteresting clergyman

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
plain means ordinary and unexciting

explanation.surface: Tea is served to a rather dull vicar.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergy member attached to an institution such as a college, hospital or regiment.

clue.text: Where ships may be refitted to cut off three feet

parts.note: to dock is to cut short, as with a tail or wages
a yard is a length of three feet

explanation.surface: A shipyard sounds like a place for chopping a ship's measurements down.
explanation.definitionFit: An area with docks and workshops where vessels are built and repaired.

clue.text: Sexy urge for Shakespeare's Percy

parts.note: hot is slang for attractive or sexy
to spur is to urge on

explanation.surface: A lustful impulse might suit a character from a Shakespeare play.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry Percy, nicknamed this, is the fiery rebel in Shakespeare's Henry IV Part 1.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of Sir Henry Percy, a character in the history plays.

clue.text: Colour of wine almost as dark as can be — little new in that

indicators.note: in that means placed inside the shortened colour word
almost means not quite complete, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: the darkest possible colour is black
N is the short form of new

explanation.surface: A wine's colour is described as nearly pitch black, with a hint of youth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims BLACK to BLAC; 'in that' puts N inside it, before the C. Blanc is French for white, as in vin blanc.
explanation.definitionFit: French white wine is vin blanc, so the colour of such wine is white in French.

clue.text: Company partner covering deficit in a really big way

indicators.note: covering means wrapped around, so the company and partner pair enclose the deficit

parts.note: an ally is a partner or associate
a deficit in accounts is a loss

explanation.surface: A firm's associate is hiding a shortfall, which is a huge business problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' treats company and partner as one pair wrapped around the deficit.
explanation.definitionFit: Hugely or enormously, from colossal meaning gigantic like the Colossus statue.

clue.text: Wanton hassles me disgracefully

indicators.note: disgracefully suggests behaving badly and out of order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone shameless pesters the speaker in disgraceful fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disgracefully' rearranges the letters of HASSLES ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Without decency or modesty, an old sense of the word wanton.

clue.text: In favour of channels showing manufactured goods

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
ducts are tubes or channels

explanation.surface: A supporter of piping displays factory-made items.
explanation.definitionFit: Things made for sale are this word's plain commercial sense.

clue.text: Seek to minimise children's games with feathers

parts.note: play is what children do for fun
down is the soft fine feathers of young birds

explanation.surface: Pillow fights with feathers flying are being downplayed.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something seem less important than it is, an idiomatic phrasal verb.

clue.text: Tell senior churchman is losing power

indicators.note: is losing means letting go of, so the abbreviation is removed from the cleric word

parts.note: a prelate is a bishop or other high-ranking cleric
P is the physics abbreviation for power

explanation.surface: Someone reports that a bishop is losing his authority.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is losing' takes the P off the front of PRELATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate or recount a story is a synonym of tell.

clue.text: Sharp hit — that is right for sharp sword

parts.note: a rap is a quick sharp knock
i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A smart blow, that is, makes the right choice of a keen weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A long slender thrusting blade used in duelling.

clue.text: Cured pork for each basket of food

parts.note: ham is cured pork from the leg of a pig
per means for each, as in per person

explanation.surface: Cured meat is portioned out for each picnic basket.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker case filled with food and treats, often given at Christmas.

clue.text: One going off to moon with odd ready-made lander finally

indicators.note: odd means strange or irregular, so the letters are put out of order
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: An astronaut heads for the moon in a quirky prefabricated landing craft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges READYMADE; 'finally' adds the last letter of 'lander'. To moon is to idle about dreamily.
explanation.definitionFit: To moon about is to drift in a reverie, which describes someone lost in fantasies.

clue.text: Sack female over anger

indicators.note: over means placed above, as the entry runs down the grid

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: A woman is dismissed after a furious row.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss someone from a job, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Social worker runs for a drink in the pub

parts.note: a worker bee lives in a social colony
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A council welfare officer heads off for a pint at the local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare professional, but it is an insect from a hive.
explanation.definitionFit: The most familiar pub drink, brewed from malt and hops.

clue.text: What shows the time clubs close securely?

parts.note: C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs
to lock is to fasten securely

explanation.surface: Nightclubs need a reliable timepiece before shutting tight at closing time.
explanation.definitionFit: A device on a wall or mantel that displays the hour.

clue.text: Last of junk IT equipment

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The final piece of scrap computer gear is going.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of gear or tools needed for an activity.

clue.text: Text summary needs English to be accurate

parts.note: a precis is a concise summary of a text

explanation.surface: A written synopsis must be in good English to count as correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact and correct in every detail is a synonym of accurate.

clue.text: US politician's south-eastern military alliance meeting resistance

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, so the definition reads as the American lawmaker is

parts.note: NATO is the North Atlantic Treaty Organization
R is the physics symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: An American politician from the south-east meets opposition from a military pact.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Senate, the upper house of Congress.

clue.text: Stick a blade into small fruit

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a pear is a common fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is cutting into a little piece of fruit with a knife.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce with a pointed weapon, the verb sense of the noun for a lance.
